clue.text: Where spirits too are low? Surely not

definitions.text: Where spirits too are low? Surely not

parts.words: Where spirits too are low? Surely not
parts.note: a cool underground store for bottles of claret and port, where the 'spirits' are drink and 'low' means below ground, not gloomy

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a place is so dismal that even ghosts feel downcast, then dismisses the idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirits' and 'low' read as mood; here they are liquor kept below ground level, and 'Surely not' hints that it is wine, not spirits, that is mostly stored there.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement storeroom for bottles of claret and port sits below ground and holds drink.

clue.text: He has a way with him, we are told

definitions.text: He has a way with him, we are told

parts.words: He has a way with him, we are told
parts.note: a man with a way about him has a trick or lure he uses on people, and the word for such a trick sounds like the 'while' of 'while away'

explanation.surface: Gossip reports that a certain man is very charming.
explanation.walkthrough: A charming man 'has a way with him', i.e. he has a ruse; 'we are told' points to sound, since this word for a ruse is heard as 'while', as in 'while away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or trick is a cunning way of getting round someone.

clue.text: Not necessarily unsound

parts.note: 'unsound' usually means faulty, but read literally it means making no sound, and something silent need not be faulty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsound' tempts as 'unreliable'; the clue says something soundless is not necessarily faulty.
explanation.definitionFit: Something silent makes no sound, without that meaning it is defective.

clue.text: Military nuclear force

parts.note: 'nuclear' here means forming a nucleus: a small core of trained soldiers around which a larger army is built, not atomic weapons

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuclear force' suggests atomic weapons, but here it is the nucleus of trained officers and men round which a regiment can be expanded.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent core group of trained personnel forms the nucleus that a larger force is built around.

clue.text: They are responsible for fixing charges

definitions.text: They are responsible for fixing charges

parts.words: They are responsible for fixing charges
parts.note: the 'charges' are the powder and shot put into a gun, not prices, and these people put them in place

explanation.surface: Some people are accused of rigging fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing charges' sounds like setting prices; it means putting the charge into a gun, the job of a shooter's attendant at a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendants at a shoot who put cartridges into guns are the ones handling the charges.

clue.text: Their's is no colourless existence

parts.note: 'colourless' seems to mean dull, but read literally these people's lives are full of paint and colour

explanation.surface: Some people lead exciting, vivid lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colourless' means dull in the surface; literally, painters work with colour all day.
explanation.definitionFit: Painters spend their working lives with pigments and colours.

clue.text: It's a return in 1ac.

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters of the words it's a are read backwards

explanation.surface: Something is described as a comeback in an earlier entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the letters of 'It's a' backwards. The definition points to 1 across: this Italian sparkling wine is the kind of thing found in the wine store there.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian sparkling white is one of the bottles likely to be kept in a cellar.

clue.text: It has wings and flies dramatically

definitions.text: It has wings and flies dramatically

parts.words: It has wings and flies dramatically
parts.note: wings and flies sound like a bird or insect, but in the theatre the wings are the side spaces and the flies the space above the boards

explanation.surface: A bird or insect soars spectacularly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wings' and 'flies' suggest a bird; 'dramatically' says they are theatre terms, the side areas and the loft above the acting area.
explanation.definitionFit: The platform in a theatre where actors perform has side wings and a fly tower above.

clue.text: O.T. type, least likely to be found in a Friendly Society

definitions.text: O.T. type, least likely to be found in a Friendly Society

parts.words: O.T. type, least likely to be found in a Friendly Society
parts.note: an Old Testament figure whose 'hand will be against every man', so the descendant of Abraham's outcast son is the last person to join a friendly society

explanation.surface: An Old Testament character would be out of place in a mutual-aid club.
explanation.walkthrough: A Friendly Society is a British mutual insurance club. Genesis says of Abraham's son by Hagar that 'his hand will be against every man', so his descendants are the type of the unfriendly outcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A descendant of Abraham's banished son, and so figuratively an outcast at odds with everyone.

clue.text: Seaside resort new in another County

definitions.text: Seaside resort new in another County

parts.words: Seaside resort new in another County
parts.note: the famous Sussex resort shares its name with a 'New' resort in a different county, on the Wirral in Cheshire

explanation.surface: A recently built resort lies in a different county.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the Sussex resort on England's south coast; with 'New' in front it names another seaside resort, New Brighton on the Wirral, in Cheshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A large seaside town on the south coast of England, in Sussex.

clue.text: When the last —— of Ravens-wood to Ravenswood shall ride" (Scott)

definitions.text: When the last —— of Ravens-wood to Ravenswood shall ride" (Scott)

parts.words: When the last —— of Ravens-wood to Ravenswood shall ride" (Scott)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor: the missing word is the Scots title for a landed proprietor

explanation.surface: A line of prophecy from a Walter Scott novel with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: The prophecy in Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor begins 'When the last Laird of Ravenswood to Ravenswood shall ride'; the gap takes the Scottish word for the owner of an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a landed estate is given this title, as the master of Ravenswood is.

clue.text: The consequence of upsetting a hamfatter

indicators.note: upsetting knocks something over and into disorder, so the letters of hamfatter are rearranged

explanation.surface: Disturbing a poor ham actor has repercussions.
explanation.walkthrough: A hamfatter is a third-rate actor; 'upsetting' rearranges its nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftereffects or results following an event are its consequence.

clue.text: " Whistle-stop " types ?

parts.note: a whistle-stop is a brief halt on a tour, but here officials blow a whistle to stop play

explanation.walkthrough: A whistle-stop tour makes brief halts; read literally, these sports officials stop the game with a whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: Match officials blow the whistle to halt play.

clue.text: She has great potential

indicators.note: potential is what something could become, so the letters of great can be made into another word

explanation.surface: A woman shows great promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' signals that the letters of 'great' can become something else, a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, as in the film star Garbo, can stand for a female 'she'.

clue.text: But his business might still be expanding

definitions.text: But his business might still be expanding

parts.words: But his business might still be expanding
parts.note: his trade is named after shrinking, yet a builder who takes on jobs may well have a growing firm

explanation.surface: A tradesman's firm keeps growing despite everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'But' sets up a paradox: his job title suggests shrinking, yet a builder who takes on contracts can still be growing his firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder or tradesman who takes on work under agreed terms runs a firm that may grow.

clue.text: Handled by those in key positions ?

definitions.text: Handled by those in key positions ?

parts.words: Handled by those in key positions ?
parts.note: key positions suggests important jobs, but tins and bottles are opened with handled tools, and cricket's first batsmen hold key places

explanation.surface: Matters are dealt with by people in senior roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key positions' suggests senior posts; literally, tin and bottle tools are held in the hand, and a key is itself one of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Tools for prising lids off tins or bottles, and keys too, unlock or open things.

clue.text: A lift over the Atlantic

parts.note: this suggests a flight across the ocean, but means what the Americans, across the Atlantic, call a lift

explanation.surface: Someone gets a ride across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lift over the Atlantic' suggests a transatlantic flight; it means the American word for a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: In American English the passenger car moving between floors of a building has this name.

clue.text: Carried at a snail's pace, according to Jaques

definitions.text: Carried at a snail's pace, according to Jaques

parts.words: Carried at a snail's pace, according to Jaques
parts.note: Jaques's 'seven ages' speech in As You Like It describes the whining schoolboy creeping like a snail to school with his school bag

explanation.surface: Something is borne along very slowly, so a Shakespeare character says.
explanation.walkthrough: In As You Like It, Jaques's 'All the world's a stage' speech has 'the whining schoolboy, with his satchel ... creeping like snail unwillingly to school'.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bag with a shoulder strap is what the schoolboy carries.

clue.text: Odd paths made in London

indicators.note: odd means strange or out of the ordinary, so the letters of paths made are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: Strange footpaths have been laid out in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd' rearranges the letters of PATHS and MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of north London known for its heath is a place in the capital.

clue.text: Ornamental hangers-on

parts.note: hangers-on are usually sycophants, but here decorative tufts of threads dangle from cushions and curtains

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangers-on' are usually followers; here they are decorative things that literally hang on.
explanation.definitionFit: Tufts of loose threads hang from curtains and cushions as decoration.

clue.text: Where a miner might be worth his salt ?

definitions.text: Where a miner might be worth his salt ?

parts.words: Where a miner might be worth his salt ?
parts.note: worth his salt means competent, but here a convict exiled to the salt mines of a cold Russian region literally works for salt

explanation.surface: A question about where a mine worker could prove his worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worth his salt' means competent; literally, exiles were sent to the salt mines of this region of Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast region of northern Asian Russia, long a place of exile and forced labour in mines.

clue.text: Make free with this word

parts.note: make free with usually means take liberties, but here the word itself means to set a slave free, from Latin for sending out of one's hand

explanation.surface: Someone takes liberties with a particular term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make free with' usually means use without permission; here 'Make free' is the meaning, release from slavery, from Latin manu mittere, 'to send from the hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: To release someone from slavery is to emancipate or liberate them.

clue.text: Battle colour

definitions.meaning: an 1859 fight in northern Italy between French-Sardinian and Austrian armies

explanation.definitionFit: Magenta in northern Italy was the site of an 1859 battle, and the bright purplish-red dye discovered that year was named after it.

clue.text: One letter you can bet on to make many more

definitions.text: One letter you can bet on to make many more

parts.words: One letter you can bet on to make many more
parts.note: bet on sounds like gambling, but put 'bet' on after the first Greek letter and you get the full set of letters

explanation.surface: A gambling tip on a sure winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bet on' sounds like gambling; literally, add BET to this Greek letter and you get ALPHABET, the full set of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of the Greek script, which with 'bet' after it names the whole set of letters.

clue.text: Not for those who don't want to get their feet wet ?

definitions.text: Not for those who don't want to get their feet wet ?

parts.words: Not for those who don't want to get their feet wet ?
parts.note: the light dancing shoes are no good in puddles, and the water-raising machines are for those who do want water

explanation.surface: Advice that something is unsuitable for the cautious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get their feet wet' means try something new; literally, thin plimsolls or dancing shoes let water in.
explanation.definitionFit: Light thin-soled shoes for dancing or gym are no protection in wet weather.

clue.text: He can hardly be commended for his ringcraft

definitions.text: He can hardly be commended for his ringcraft

parts.words: He can hardly be commended for his ringcraft
parts.note: ringcraft is a boxer's skill, but here the rings are wedding rings, too many of them

explanation.surface: A boxer gets poor marks for his skill in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringcraft' is a boxer's skill; here the rings are wedding rings, and this man has married twice at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who marries a second wife while still married to the first.

clue.text: Port or coffee ?

definitions.meaning: a harbour town on the Red Sea coast of Yemen
a fine Arabian coffee, or a drink of coffee and chocolate

explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a Red Sea harbour in Yemen, and the fine Arabian coffee once shipped from it took its name.

clue.text: Q's was splendid, albeit novel

parts.note: Q was the pen name of Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch, whose novel The Splendid ... is completed by the word wanted

explanation.surface: Someone praises a new idea as splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: Q is the pen name of Sir Arthur Quiller-Couch, whose 1889 novel was The Splendid Spur; 'novel' means a book, not 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked device on a rider's heel, the item named in the title of Q's adventure novel.

clue.text: Rumba? No, it is another dance altogether

indicators.note: another signals a different arrangement, so the letters of Rumba, No and it make something else

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a guess: that's not a rumba, it's a quite different dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another ... altogether' rearranges the letters of RUMBA, NO and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively old Provençal dance accompanied by a drum.

clue.text: The inexpensive side

parts.note: add 'side' to a word for inexpensive and you get a famous street in the City of London

explanation.walkthrough: Cheapside is a historic street in the City of London; the answer is the word that comes before 'side'.
explanation.definitionFit: Low in price, this word joined to 'side' names a London street.

clue.text: Girl who couldn't be kept down ?

definitions.meaning: a female first name taken from a flower
got up or came back up: the past tense of rise

explanation.definitionFit: Rose is a girl's name, and it is also the past tense of rise, what something that would not stay down did.

clue.text: Alan's dream is to become amphibian

indicators.note: to become means to change into something else, so the letters of Alan's and dream are rearranged

parts.note: the name with its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A man named Alan longs to be a frog or newt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become' rearranges the letters of ALANS and DREAM; here the possessive S counts as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A newt-like creature living on land and in water, once fabled to live in fire.
